cues.en: In Rome, in the year 1590, the Italian priest, Lorenzo Busnardo, a well-known chess master, faced off against an opponent whose name is now lost to time. Now, not only is this game a lot of fun, it's also one of the earliest chess games ever recorded using modern rules, and therefore a fantastic factual document. Let me take a few seconds to show you why this game is so great. Busnardo, plain white, opens with King pawn to e4. Black responds, King pawn to e5.
cues.zh: 1590年的罗马，意大利神父 Lorenzo Busnardo——一位著名的国际象棋大师，对上了一位姓名已不可考的对手。这局棋不仅极具趣味，还是有记录以来最早采用现代规则的棋局之一，是一份绝佳的史料。让我花几秒钟带大家看看它有多精彩。执白的 Busnardo 起手走王前兵 e4，黑棋跟走王前兵 e5。

cues.en: White develops the knight to f3, black plays knight to c6. White then plays bishop c4, a sequence we now call the Italian game, which is the fastest way to open up these two squares, allowing the king to castle safely on the right-hand side of the board. Black responds with bishop c5. Next follows c3, which blocks the knight from moving to b4, while also preparing for a pawn attack on d4. And now for the first notable move of the game, queen to e7.
cues.zh: 白棋出马到 f3，黑棋跳马到 c6。接着白棋走象 c4，这就是我们现在常说的“意大利开局”，也是清空这两个格子最快的方式，可以让王安全地在棋盘右侧进行易位。黑棋应以象 c5。接着白棋走 c3，既封堵了黑马跳到 b4 的路线，又为兵冲 d4 做准备。接下来是本局第一个值得关注的一步：后走到 e7。

cues.en: It seems Black is thinking too much about the battle that's going to take place in the center of the board, and not enough in getting the King safely castled. A better move would have been pawn to d6, which allows for the development of the bishop, or knight f6. For his part, Busanardo now castles, keeping the King safely tucked away here. Black's next move is pawn d6. Now, with a small tempo advantage, White begins the attack, bringing the pawn to d4, threatening to capture the bishop.
cues.zh: 看起来黑棋把太多精力放在了即将爆发的中心区域争夺上，而没有优先保证王的安全易位。更好的选择原本是走兵到 d6 便于出象，或是出马到 f6。Busnardo 此时选择易位，把王妥善保护在这里。黑棋下一步走了兵 d6。凭借微弱的先手优势，白棋开始进攻，挺兵到 d4，威胁吃黑象。

cues.en: Black wisely moves the bishop back to B6 to maintain control over this important diagonal, but by being forced to move the same piece twice in the opening, he's lost the opportunity to bring this knight or bishop out into the fray, which leaves the king still exposed in the centre of the board for yet another move. White now develops his bishop to G5, attacking the queen who can't attack back because the bishop is defended by this knight. And for anyone who might not know, a queen for a bishop is a terrible trade. Instead, Black decides to counter-attack with pawn to F6.
cues.zh: 黑棋明智地将象退到 b6，以维持对这条关键斜线的控制；但开局被迫连动同一枚棋子，让他失去了把马或象调入战局的机会，导致王在棋盘中央又多暴露了一回合。白棋随后出象到 g5 抓后，黑后无法反击，因为白象受到白马的保护。可能有人不知道，用后换象是非常亏的。于是，黑棋决定挺兵到 f6 反击。

cues.zh: 在和声可读性与节奏可读性之间。当横向间距统一时，节奏更易读。但如果你引入各种音符和和弦，为了看清它们——包括这些升号和降号——就需要额外空间，这必然会破坏横向统一性。如果你做成这样就更糟。现在第3小节宽度是第1小节的两倍，尽管两者持续时间相同。

cues.en: Now, logically, you'd imagine that the answer is to space everything out to be uniform. But that then means that loads of space has been taken up unnecessarily, so less overall music can fit on the page or screen, which is awkward for performers who now have to do more page turns. And this push and pull between different musical criteria is emblematic of the balance that musical notation needs to strike. Except, it needs to strike this balance in about a hundred different ways. As I've said, it's a multi-layered compromise.
cues.zh: 那么按逻辑，你会以为答案是把所有内容都均匀拉开。但这意味着大量空间被不必要地占用，于是页面或屏幕上能容纳的乐谱总量更少，这对演奏者很麻烦，因为他们现在得翻更多页。而这种不同音乐标准之间的拉扯，正体现了音乐记谱法需要取得的平衡。只不过，它需要在大约一百种不同维度上取得这种平衡。正如我说过的，这是一种多层次的妥协。

cues.en: which means that when you view one aspect of notation in isolation, you will find imperfections. And this is what gives endless fuel to critics who advocate for outright replacement. For me, it's not logical. Now, these critics can be split into a few camps. I'm going to name the first camp the Reformers, a small group of highly informed and imaginative people who've proposed alternative notation systems of their own, some of which challenge Western notation in really compelling ways, as we'll see later.
cues.zh: 这意味着，当你孤立地看记谱法的某一个方面时，总会发现不完美之处。而这给主张彻底替换的批评者提供了无尽弹药。对我来说，这不合逻辑。这些批评者可以分为几个阵营。我把第一个阵营叫作改革派，一小群知识渊博、富有想象力的人，他们提出了自己的替代记谱系统，其中一些以非常有力的方式挑战西方记谱法，后面我们会看到。

cues.en: Next are the C minus reformers, a much larger group of reasonably informed musicians who exhibit a deep knowledge in one area, but who are blind to many others. Then there are the disruptors, a group of highly uninformed people, often with expertise in a different field, usually technology, who mistake their ignorance for a kind of fresh-eyed clarity, misrecognizing the gaps in their understanding as actual gaps in notation itself, things musicians just forgot to address because they're so silly.
cues.zh: 接下来是C-改革派，一个大得多的群体，都是有一定见识的音乐家，在某一领域有深入知识，却对其他许多领域视而不见。然后是颠覆者，一群非常无知的人，常常在其他领域有专长，通常是技术领域，他们把自己的无知误认为一种初生牛犊般的清晰视野，把自身理解中的空白误认为记谱法本身的空白，觉得那是音乐家太傻了才忘了处理的问题。

cues.en: The disruptors can see that the emperor isn't wearing any clothes, and they're gonna make themselves heard, loudly denouncing music notation as hopelessly stupid and inefficient. It brings to mind the age-old saying. The less you know about a subject, the more you bitch and moan about it like a petulant brat. To give an example, let's look at a tweet by the founder of Epic Games, Tim Sweeney.
cues.zh: 颠覆者能看出皇帝没穿衣服，而且他们会让自己被听见，大声谴责音乐记谱法愚蠢低效到无可救药。这让人想起那句老话。你对一个主题了解得越少，就越像个任性的小屁孩一样抱怨个没完。举个例子，我们来看看 Epic Games 创始人 Tim Sweeney 的一条推文。

cues.en: Now, as eager as I am to be schooled by a video game developer on the productive use of my time, Tim has not really made the most convincing argument here. But in order to show why, we need to take a step back, way back, baby, to look at how musical notation came to be this way, so we can catalog its long list of crimes and also give ourselves a proper historical context, which will help us have more fun when assessing the suggestions of those who would see it replaced. This will also give those who can't read notation a quick tutorial on how it works too.
cues.zh: 尽管我很渴望被一位电子游戏开发者教导如何高效利用时间，但 Tim 在这里并没有提出最有说服力的论点。但为了说明为什么，我们需要退一步，退得远远的，宝贝，来看看音乐记谱法是如何变成现在这样的，这样我们就能整理出它的一长串罪状，也给自己一个恰当的历史背景，这有助于我们在评估那些想取代它的人的建议时更有乐趣。这也会给不会读谱的人一个关于它如何运作的快速教程。

cues.en: The Belgian musicologist Francois-Auguste Hivert suggests that of all the various systems of music notation that have existed throughout history, there are two fundamentally different types. The first is phonetic notation, where sounds are represented by letters, numbers, or words. We can see this in traditional Chinese, Arabic, and Indian notation, as well as ancient Greek notation. We can also see it in more modern examples like the tonic sol fa system or the Chinese system jianpu.
cues.zh: 比利时音乐学家 Francois-Auguste Hivert 提出，历史上存在过的各种记谱体系中，有两类根本不同的类型。第一类是表音记谱法，用字母、数字或词语来表示声音。我们在传统中国、阿拉伯和印度记谱法中能看到这一点，在古希腊记谱法中也能看到。在更现代的例子里也能看到，比如 tonic sol-fa 体系或中国的 jianpu（简谱）。

cues.en: Let's zoom in on ancient Greece for a moment to give you a feel for how unique this system was. Here's an example of a fragment of ancient music where you can see the words of a poem with precise musical pitches described in lettering above them. There were actually two lettering systems, one for voice and one for instrumentalists. It's important to know a little bit about how the Greeks thought about music because it helps us understand why their notation system was so simple. First, melody was everything to the Greeks. Harmony, what Aristotle called mixis,
cues.zh: 让我们暂时聚焦古希腊，感受一下这套体系有多独特。这里有一段古希腊音乐残片，你能看到诗中的词，上方用字母标出了精确的音高。实际上有两套字母体系，一套用于人声，一套用于器乐。稍微了解希腊人如何看待音乐很重要，因为这能帮我们理解为什么他们的记谱体系如此简单。首先，旋律对希腊人来说就是一切。和声，也就是亚里士多德所说的 mixis，

cues.en: was often really simple compared to what we're used to today, chosen carefully so that it didn't overly influence the colour or character of the melody. For example, listen to this fragment of melody. Now listen to this accompanying harmony and observe how simple it is and how it doesn't compete with the melody. If we were to apply a modern harmonic accompaniment to that melody, it might sound a bit more like this. That would be alien to the Greeks. Harmony was subject to strict rules and only certain pairings of notes were considered acceptable.
cues.zh: 与我们今天习惯的相比，往往非常简单，而且是精心选择的，以免过度影响旋律的色彩或特征。例如，听这段旋律。再听这个伴奏和声，注意它有多简单，以及它如何不与旋律争锋。如果我们给那段旋律配上现代和声伴奏，听起来可能更像这样。那对希腊人来说会很陌生。和声受严格规则约束，只有某些音符搭配才被认为可以接受。

cues.en: It was taken so seriously that in Plato's Republic, he advised young students to keep away from accompaniment altogether. They should just sing the same notes that they're playing, because anything more detailed than that could corrupt their character, or the character of other listeners. Proper accompaniment was only to be attempted by professionals. With vocal music, rhythm was based on how words and syllables were spoken. However, for instrumental music, they couldn't rely on the system, so created symbols to reflect duration instead. A regular unit of time was called a short.
cues.zh: 这件事被看得如此严肃，以至于在柏拉图的《理想国》里，他建议年轻学生完全远离伴奏。他们应该只唱自己正在演奏的那些音，因为任何比这更复杂的东西都可能败坏他们的品性，或其他听众的品性。像样的伴奏只能由专业人士尝试。对于声乐，节奏基于词和音节被说出的方式。然而，对于器乐，他们不能依赖这套体系，于是创造符号来反映时值。一个常规的时间单位叫作“短”。

cues.en: which is what we'd call an eighth note. Since it was the default, it didn't need a symbol, which was great when you knew that rule, but caused quite a headache for later historians trying to decipher how the system worked. Anyway, apart from the short, you had the long, which was two shorts in duration, then the three times long, then the four times long, etc. Remember this point because it's going to come back several times. Today, we conceptualize scales as a division of the octave. However, the Greeks didn't. They considered the fundamental unit of pitch organization to be the tetrachord.
cues.zh: 也就是我们今天所说的八分音符。由于它是默认单位，所以不需要符号；知道这条规则时很棒，但后来试图破译这套体系如何运作的历史学家却为此很头疼。总之，除了短音符，还有长音符，时值为两个短音符，然后是三倍长、四倍长，等等。记住这一点，因为它后面还会多次出现。今天，我们把音阶理解为八度的划分。然而，希腊人并不这样想。他们认为音高组织的基本单位是四音列。

cues.en: which is a series of four ascending notes spanning a perfect fourth. The first note of the first tetra chord was called the hypate, which translates to the highest. The next note in the tetra chord was called the par-hypate, which means the next highest and so on. This can be super confusing for us because we use words like high and above today to refer to pitch. This note is above this note, etc. But the hypate was actually the lowest pitch in a tetra chord. So when they say highest, what they actually mean is closer to tallest.
cues.zh: 也就是跨越纯四度的连续四个上行音。第一个四音列（tetrachord）的首个音被称为 hypate，翻译过来就是“最高”。四音列中的下一个音叫 par-hypate，意思是“次高”，以此类推。这对我们来说可能会非常令人困惑，因为我们今天用“高”和“上”等词来指代音高，比如这个音在那个音上方等等。但 hypate 实际上是四音列中音高最低的音。所以当他们说“最高”时，实际意思其实更接近于“最长”或“最高大”。

cues.en: Specifically, it's referring to the string on the lyre the highpate was played on, which was longer than all the others. The ancient Greeks did not conceptualise pitch as something that could be higher or lower, so the idea of representing pitch vertically would have made no sense to them. I'm not going to dig into ancient Greek music any further than this, since ancient sources are both rare and also contradictory. It seems that, just like today, everyone had a different opinion. So let's zoom back out and focus on the other fundamental type of notation defined by Hebert.
cues.zh: 具体来说，它指的是里拉琴（lyre）上演奏 hypate 的那根琴弦，它比其他所有弦都要长。古希腊人并没有把音高概念化为可以“更高”或“更低”的东西，因此用垂直空间来表示音高对他们来说毫无意义。古希腊音乐我就不再深入探讨了，因为古代文献既稀少又相互矛盾。看起来就像今天一样，每个人都有不同的看法。所以让我们把视野拉远，聚焦于 Hebert 定义的另一种基本记谱法类型。

cues.en: Diastemic notation, where the upward and downward movement of a pitch is represented vertically using abstract symbols. For example, Ethiopian, Byzantine, Armenian, and Jewish liturgical notation, as well as the Noom system seen in Gregorian chant, and of course, the system we use today. The word diastema comes from the Greek word meaning interval, which is incidentally a word also used to describe the gap between your teeth. Now, what better way to understand diastemic notation than by looking at how the system we use today came into existence?
cues.zh: 间距记谱法（Diastemic notation），即用抽象符号在垂直方向上表示音高的升降。例如埃塞俄比亚、拜占庭、亚美尼亚和犹太礼拜记谱法，以及格里高利圣咏中出现的纽姆符（Neume）系统，当然还有我们今天使用的记谱系统。diastema 这个词来自希腊语，意思是“音程”，顺便提一句，这个词也用来指牙缝。那么，想要理解间距记谱法，还有什么比探究我们今天使用的系统是如何诞生的更好的方式呢？

cues.en: So grab your popcorn folks, because we've now reached the part of the video where I do the history of Western notation. The ancient Greek notation we just looked at had persisted under the Roman Empire until the 4th century. Greek culture was having a hard time. The Christian church rejected many aspects of Greek music, including the use of the lyre and flute, because they were associated with pagan worship. The final blow to Greek music came when the Emperor Theodosius, an ardent Christian, closed all remaining pagan schools.
cues.zh: 所以大家拿好爆米花，因为视频已经来到了讲述西方记谱法历史的部分。我们刚才看到的古希腊记谱法在罗马帝国统治下一直延续到了4世纪。当时希腊文化的处境很艰难。基督教会排斥希腊音乐的诸多方面，包括里拉琴和长笛的使用，因为它们与异教崇拜相关。对希腊音乐的致命一击，是狂热的基督教徒 Theodosius 皇帝关闭了所有残存的异教学校。

cues.en: Any Greek notation that was still being taught at the time stopped, and ancient Greek music died out entirely. And for a time, there was no musical notation in the Western Christian world. Liturgical music, known as plain chant or plain song, was passed down by ear. There is one legend of a notated book of sacred music which was collected by Gregory the Great, poked between 590 and 604. It was called the Antiphonary, which was supposedly chained to the altar of St. Peter's Cathedral. So even if it did exist, which is unlikely, no one had access to it.
cues.zh: 当时仍在传授的所有希腊记谱法就此终止，古希腊音乐彻底消亡。在随后的很长一段时间里，西方基督教世界没有任何乐谱。被称为素歌（plainchant 或 plainsong）的礼拜音乐全靠口耳相传。有一个传说是，Gregory the Great（教皇任期为 590 至 604 年）曾收集整理过一本带有记谱的圣乐书。它被称为 Antiphonary，据说被铁链锁在 St. Peter's Cathedral 的祭坛上。所以即便它真的存在过——虽然这不太可能——也根本没人能接触到它。

cues.en: Incidentally, Gregory is the person being referred to when we talk about Gregorian chant. Anyway, throughout the Christian world, a large problem was beginning to emerge, a total lack of consistency in how plain chant was performed from region to region. This came to a head in the 9th century when a dispute emerged between the Frankish and Roman churches, documented by the Aquitainean monk and musicologist Adémarque de Chabane. Behold, a dispute arose during the feast days of Easter among the cantors of the Romans and the Gauls.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，我们常说的“格里高利圣咏”，名字就来源于这位 Gregory。不管怎样，当时整个基督教世界开始浮现出一个大问题：各地的素歌唱法完全缺乏统一性。这一矛盾在 9 世纪彻底爆发，法兰克教会和罗马教会之间产生了分歧，阿基坦僧侣兼音乐学者 Adémarque de Chabane 对此进行了记录：“瞧，在复活节庆典期间，罗马唱诗班与高卢唱诗班之间爆发了一场争端。”

cues.en: The Gauls said that they sang better and more beautifully than the Romans, and the Romans claimed that they performed the ecclesiastical songs in a most learned way, just as they had been taught by St. Gregory the Pope, and that the Gauls sang corruptly, and lacerated the correct song by destroying it. According to the modern musicologist James Greer, this dispute was eventually resolved in favour of the Romans by the Emperor Charlemagne, whose administration then launched a policy of musical standardization to ensure that everyone else followed suit.
cues.zh: 高卢人称自己唱得比罗马人更好听，而罗马人则声称自己才是最正统地遵照教皇 St. Gregory 所传授的方式演唱圣歌，还指责高卢人唱法拙劣，严重毁坏了正确的圣歌。根据现代音乐学家 James Greer 的说法，这场争端最终由 Charlemagne 大帝裁定罗马人胜出，随后其统治机构推行了一项音乐标准化政策，以确保所有人步调一致。

cues.en: As a result, new documentation was created to specify what liturgical repositories should be performed, and more importantly, for our purposes, how they should be performed. This is quite probably when the first type of notation, referred to as pneumatic notation, was invented. And it was crap. Initially, nooms were little squiggles that sat above the words of a chant to give the singer a sense of melodic direction. In terms of pitch, this notation indicated whether the singer should go up or down, but it wasn't very precise.
cues.zh: 因此，官方制定了新文献，明确规定该演唱哪些礼仪曲目，而更重要的是——对我们而言——该怎么演唱。这很可能就是第一种记谱法，即纽姆记谱法（pneumatic notation）诞生的时刻。但它烂透了。最初，纽姆符只是写在歌词上方的一些扭曲小符号，给歌手提供旋律走向的参考。在音高上，它能指出是该升高还是降低，但极不精确。

cues.en: and was mainly used for jogging your memory, you still needed to be taught the song first. Rhythm was not notated at this point. Like the vocal music of Ancient Greece, it was instead derived from the syllables of the words that were sung. One fun thing about this notation was how it visualized the common practice of lengthening certain words for dramatic effect by placing additional nooms between syllables. Take this example of a fairly extreme lengthening of the word jubilate. Early pneumatic notation proved too vague and open to interpretation. As I already mentioned,
cues.zh: 它主要是用来唤起记忆，你还是得先由人教会这首歌。此时节奏完全没有记录。就像古希腊声乐一样，节奏完全源自所唱词句的音节。这种记谱法有个有趣的地方：当时为了戏剧效果常会拉长某些词，而它通过在音节之间添加额外的纽姆符，将这种做法可视化了。以这个把 jubilate 一词拉得极长的例子为例。早期的纽姆记谱法被证明过于模糊，解释空间太大。正如我刚才所说，

cues.en: It was mainly used as a memory aid and was therefore useless for learning newly composed music, which still required direct instruction. And so, it gradually became obvious to many people that a more precise system was needed. This was the technical and creative challenge of the day, and it didn't have an obvious solution. Around 930 or 940 AD, a treatise of unknown authorship proposed a system we now call Dacian notation, which was part of an effort to fuse ancient Greek music theory with the music of the time. Pitch intervals were described vertically,
cues.zh: 它主要用作备忘辅助，对于学习新谱写的音乐毫无用处，学新歌依然需要当面指导。因此，许多人逐渐意识到需要一套更精确的系统。这是当时的技术与创造性难题，并没有现成的解决办法。大约在公元 930 或 940 年，一篇佚名专著提出了一套我们现在称作达西亚记谱法（Dacian notation）的系统，试图将古希腊音乐理论与当时的音乐相融合。音程在垂直方向上展开表示，

cues.en: tone, semitone, tone, etc. from the lowest to the highest note. And the words to be sung would move up and down between these intervals to indicate exact pitch. This example shows how the parts of four different singers could be displayed at the same time, making it the first ever example of notated polyphonic music. However, this system wasn't taken up. There were many other attempted reforms around the same time period, which we're unfortunately going to have to skip through. This takes us to what is probably the most celebrated breakthrough in notation.
cues.zh: 从最低音到最高音依次排列为全音、半音、全音等。待唱的歌词则在这些音程间上下浮动，以标明确切的音高。这个例子展示了如何同时展示四位不同歌手的声部，使其成为有史以来首个记录下来的复调音乐范例。然而，这套系统并没有被普及采纳。同一时期还有许多其他改革尝试，可惜我们只能略过了。接下来，我们将迎来记谱法史上可能最著名的一次重大突破。

cues.en: In the 11th century, the Benedictine monk Guido Overetso proposed a new system, which synthesised many earlier ideas. Guido was, by all accounts, a man of great genius, who also had a super sharp tongue. He hated pneumatic notation for its imprecision and didn't have many good things to say about teachers of vocal music, who, due to the limitations of pneumatic notation, were unable to sing newly composed music. In his treatise on sight singing, he summarised the situation like this. For most people,
cues.zh: 11 世纪，本笃会修士 Guido Overetso 提出了一套新体系，综合了许多早期想法。无论从哪方面看，Guido 都是个天才，同时也极其毒舌。他厌恶纽姆记谱法的不精确，对声乐教师也没多少好话——由于纽姆记谱法的局限，他们唱不了新创作的乐曲。在他关于视唱的论著中，他这样总结当时的情况。对大多数人来说，

cues.en: When they learn an art from their teacher, it provides a basis upon which other skills are learned. When little boys develop the skills to read, they go on to read other books. But these singing masters and their pupils, even if they sang every day for 100 years, they'd still not be able to sing a new composition without prior manual instruction. Consequently, the time they waste with their wretched singing would be enough to learn the contents of all the books in the world, both sacred and secular. Just goes to show. However musical practice may change over the centuries,

Now, if you return to disrupt your Tim Sweeney's tweet and follow on tweets, clefs are, in his opinion, one of the major crimes of notation, which his proposed solution, the piano roll, fixes because the full range is always exposed, so no need for clefs. Now, I use the piano roll for producing music all the time.
cues.zh: 有一套叫谱号的符号，用来表示你正在看整体音域的哪一段，这样就能排除无关部分。比如这个高音谱号表示你看这里。这个低音谱号表示你看这里。现在，回到 Tim Sweeney 那条推文和后续推文的讨论串，在他看来，谱号是记谱法的主要罪状之一，而他提出的解决方案——钢琴卷帘——解决了这个问题，因为完整音域始终可见，不需要谱号。我一直用钢琴卷帘来制作音乐。

cues.en: I couldn't really do without it. But is it a better system for reading music? Well, not really. It's kind of hard to know where to start here, but let's start with Tim's smug assumption that by championing the piano roll, he's doing away with the old and bringing in the new, because this idea is not even remotely close to new. On the contrary, it's been proposed numerous times over the last two centuries. The first documented proposal of this idea was by Carl Christian Friedrich Krauss in 1811.
cues.zh: 我真的离不开它。但它真是更好的读谱系统吗？其实并不是。这里有点不知从何说起，但先看 Tim 那个自鸣得意的假设：他推崇钢琴卷帘，是在除旧布新，因为这个想法根本一点都不新。相反，过去两个世纪里它被提出过很多次。有文献记载的最早提出者是 Carl Christian Friedrich Krauss，1811 年。

cues.en: Although it failed to make any impact, it was remarkably innovative for its time. Like the modern piano roll, the entire playable range is displayed, removing the need for clefs. The duration of notes was represented not by symbols, but by linear rectangles. He argued that this was way more visually intuitive. A quarter note would look like this, a half note, or a minim, which is twice as long, would look like this, and so on. This is a concept the composer and music scholar Gardner Reed observed
cues.zh: 虽然它没产生什么影响，但在当时极具创新性。和现代钢琴卷帘一样，它显示了整个可演奏音域，因而不再需要谱号。音符时值不用符号表示，而用长条矩形表示。他认为这在视觉上直观得多。四分音符会是这样，二分音符，也就是 minim，长度是四分音符的两倍，会是这样，以此类推。这是作曲家兼音乐学者 Gardner Reed 观察到的一个概念

cues.en: was to be constantly rediscovered by composers and theorists throughout the 19th century and into our own time. Indeed, the idea was proposed again with some small differences by an anonymous academic in 1837, and many times again after that. It's worth mentioning that the piano roll is itself a variant of the chromatic staff idea, and just like the chromatic staff, it suffers from the same vertical interval problem. That aside, physical space in general is a problem. Using the modern piano roll as our example, how could it be used to perform a piece of music?
cues.zh: 它会在整个19世纪直至当代，被作曲家和理论家不断重新发现。确实，1837 年一位匿名学者又提出了这个想法，只有一些小差异，之后还多次被提出。值得一提的是，钢琴卷帘本身就是半音阶谱表想法的一个变体，而且和半音阶谱表一样，它也有同样的纵向音程问题。撇开这点不谈，物理空间本身也是个问题。以现代钢琴卷帘为例，它怎么能用来演奏一首乐曲呢？

cues.en: Well, let's start with printing. Still the predominant method used today by performing musicians. Clearly, no matter what way you arrange a piano roll that's this tall, a printed page is only going to hold a really small amount of music compared to standard notation. Meaning, far more page turns, far more paper, which in turn means far more rustling, movement and mistakes. Okay, printing is out. That's pretty clear. So I guess it's only fair to focus on large tablet devices instead. Oh, it's the exact same problem.
cues.zh: 那先从印刷说起。它仍是当今演奏音乐家使用的主要方式。很明显，不管你怎么排布这么高的钢琴卷帘，和标准记谱法相比，一页印刷纸能容纳的音乐都少得可怜。这意味着更多翻页、更多纸张，进而意味着更多窸窣声、动作和错误。好吧，印刷出局。这很清楚。那我想公平起见，应该看看大尺寸平板设备。哦，问题一模一样。

Which means the only real answer is a continuous scrolling view. Ah, here we go. Finally, I knew there was going to be some advantage that the piano roll had over. No, notation has worked in continuous view for decades. So, let's look at how durations are visualized. This tends to be one of the most beguiling reforms, because it appears to be much more obviously intuitive at first glance.
cues.zh: 屏幕上能显示的音乐少得多，这意味着要不停翻过大量页面。好吧，所以音乐家绝大多数偏好的编排方式——页面视图——也被排除了。也就是说，唯一真正的答案是连续滚动视图。啊，来了。终于，我就知道钢琴卷帘会有某种优势。不，记谱法在连续视图中已经用了几十年。那么，我们来看看时值是如何可视化的。这往往是最诱人的改革之一，因为乍一看它显然更直观。

cues.en: Tim Sweeney thinks that symbolic representation of duration is completely stupid. Adding more tail feathers to a note makes it go faster, like some sort of genetically engineered bird. Now, I hate to ruin a joke, Tim, but it's not really about speed, is it? It's about note length. They're not faster, they're shorter. I know that might seem like the same thing.
cues.zh: Tim Sweeney 认为时值的符号表示完全愚蠢。给音符加上更多尾羽会让它跑得更快，就像某种基因工程鸟。Tim，我不想破坏这个笑话，但这其实不是关于速度，对吧？这是关于音符长度。它们不是更快，而是更短。我知道这看起来可能是同一回事。

cues.en: Either system would probably work equally as well at early grades because the rhythms involved are so basic. It's just when you go beyond the absolute basics to include more nuanced rhythms that piano roll visualisation suffers. If a performer was trying to sight read this passage, they'd be forgiven for not realising that these durations and these durations are actually different, so sight reading would be much harder. These are actually toplets which are much easier to read in standard notation. The point is, relative length has to be measured and has to be judged every time.
cues.zh: 两种系统在初级程度可能同样好用，因为涉及的节奏非常基础。只是当你超越绝对基础、加入更细微的节奏时，钢琴卷帘可视化就吃亏了。如果演奏者试图视奏这一段，他们没意识到这些时值和这些时值其实不同，也是情有可原的，所以视奏会难得多。这些其实是连音符，在标准记谱法中读起来容易得多。关键是，相对长度每次都必须被测量和判断。

cues.en: Symbolic representations don't. This advantage that symbolism has over literalism is why the English language uses these abstractions rather than mouth pictograms, which one could argue are more intuitive for beginners. But we're not done. Now, as I mentioned at the start of this video, many of those who put proposals forward are not usually thinking globally. Typically, they're usually focusing on their own instrument and overwhelmingly fail to consider cases like, well, players don't always perform solo.
cues.zh: 符号表示则不必。符号化相对于字面化具有的这一优势，正是英语使用这些抽象符号、而不是嘴巴象形图的原因——有人可能会说，嘴巴象形图对初学者更直观。但我们还没完。正如我在视频开头提到的，许多提出建议的人通常不会从全局考虑。通常，他们只关注自己的乐器，绝大多数都没想到这样的情况，比如，演奏者并不总是独奏。

cues.en: Take the common case where a player wants to be able to see what another player is performing. Oh god, that means two piano rolls. Or, I guess it could be one piano roll where each performer is represented in different colours or something. Which means a piano player in a piano trio would see something like this. Composers writing for a wind ensemble would be looking at something like this. And conductors? Jesus, how on earth would you conduct this? No, it would have to be multiple piano rolls, wouldn't it? Which means he'd have to narrow the range of each piano roll to make them fit on the page.
cues.zh: 拿常见情况来说，一个演奏者想看到另一个演奏者正在演奏什么。天哪，那就意味着两个钢琴卷帘。或者，我猜也可以是一个钢琴卷帘，用不同颜色之类表示每个演奏者。这意味着钢琴三重奏里的钢琴手会看到类似这样的东西。为管乐团写作的作曲家会看到类似这样的东西。那指挥呢？天哪，这到底要怎么指挥？不，那得用多个钢琴卷帘，对吧？这意味着他必须缩窄每个钢琴卷帘的音域，才能把它们塞进页面。

cues.en: But then, oh no, since the notes here are out of view, you'd need some kind of way to scroll down to see them. Ah, that's why clefs exist, isn't it? So you can see notes in different ranges because gigantic grids are, generally speaking, incredibly impractical. So I guess you'd have to plunk another piano roll here. That's just a clef. It's a far more visually noisy clef that only pianists can read.
cues.zh: 可紧接着，糟了，因为这里的音符跑出视野了，你就得想办法向下滚动才能看见它们。啊，这就是谱号存在的原因，对吧？这样你就能看清不同音域的音符，因为一般来说，超大网格简直太不实用了。所以我想你大概得在这儿硬塞另一个钢琴卷帘。那不就是个谱号嘛。只不过是一个视觉干扰多得多、而且只有钢琴家才看得懂的谱号。

Jesus, this is hard to read. Well, I hope I've explained the benefit to you, Tim. Now, toddle off, design some more dark pattern loot boxes. Daddy'll take it from here. Now, for those who are still doubtful, just bear in mind that the piano roll is far more predominantly used in music creation today than notation. Every DAW has a piano roll, so with that in mind, you would think...
cues.zh: 高音谱号上的某个位置，跟低音谱号上的相同位置代表不同的音，这有什么好处？相隔一个八度的两个音在……天哪，这段太难念了。好吧，Tim，我希望已经给你把好处讲明白了。现在赶紧走开，再去设计几个诱导消费的开箱机制吧。剩下的交给爸爸我来。现在，对于那些仍心存疑虑的人，请记住，在当今的音乐创作中，钢琴卷帘的使用率远高于传统五线谱。每个 DAW 都有钢琴卷帘，考虑到这一点，你可能会觉得……

cues.en: that if the piano roll was suitable as a system for reading music during a performance, people would have started using it organically for that purpose by now. I threw a really quick poll on Twitter to ask whether people had ever seen it done, and the overwhelming response was, never. Those who said yes, were mainly talking about live streams of games like Guitar Hero, and we will get to Guitar Hero. And just one last thing, I have real data at my fingertips to go on too. A few years ago, just as I was joining MuseScore, there was a piano roll introduced on our sister website, MuseScore.com.
cues.zh: 如果钢琴卷帘适合作为演奏时的读谱系统，大家现在肯定早就自发这么用了。我在 Twitter 上快速发起了一个投票，问大家有没有见过有人这么干，压倒性的回答是：从没见过。那些说见过的，主要是指 Guitar Hero 这类游戏的直播，后面我们会聊到 Guitar Hero。最后还有一点，我手头也有真实数据可以佐证。几年前，就在我刚加入 MuseScore 时，我们的姐妹网站 MuseScore.com 上线了钢琴卷帘功能。

cues.en: For time, it was even set to the default view as an experiment to see whether people preferred to read music that way. It was a major failure, with almost all users switching it off and never turning it on again. Nothing about the piano roll has indicated that it's suitable for sight reading because it has just about no practical advantages and a myriad of obvious weaknesses. Now, on to the next topic. Clefs! Hold on, we just spoke about this. What's going on? Well, despite my defensive, Clefs, standard notation should not get a free pass here.
cues.zh: 有一阵子，它甚至被设为默认视图来做实验，看看大家是否更喜欢用这种方式读谱。结果是一次彻底的失败，几乎所有用户都关掉了它，而且再也没打开过。没有任何迹象表明钢琴卷帘适合视奏，因为它几乎没有任何实际优势，却有着一大堆显而易见的缺陷。现在，进入下一个话题：谱号！等等，我们刚才不是聊过这个了吗？这是怎么回事？好吧，虽然我刚才维护了谱号，但在这一点上，传统记谱法也不该被轻易放过。

cues.en: I've argued why they're required, but not whether these are the best ones possible. I mean, it's hard to make an argument that they are. It just can't be denied that there's an awkwardness to them. Specifically, because each clef displays notes differently. For example, the range C, D, E, F, G, A, B, C is here on a treble clef, but here on an alto clef, and here on a bass clef. So if you're learning an instrument that uses the treble clef, you'll soon become accustomed to the fact that C is here.
cues.zh: 我论证了为什么它们必不可少，但并没说现有的谱号就是最优解。我是说，很难去论证它们就是最好的。无可否认，它们确实有很别扭的地方。具体来说，就是每个谱号显示音符的方式都不同。比如，C、D、E、F、G、A、B、C 这一段音域，在高音谱号上是这里，但在中音谱号上是这里，而在低音谱号上又是这里。所以如果你学的是使用高音谱号的乐器，你很快就会习惯 C 在这个位置。

cues.en: and it really does screw with your head when you try to read an alto clef where C is now here. Didn't anyone think to revise this? Well, yes, thousands of times. Here's a proposal from 1672 by Reverend Thomas Salmon, which garnered a little bit of fame in its day. You have a treble clef, which uses the symbol TR, the range is G to G, then you have a mean clef, same range, then a bass clef, same range. Great! So when you learn one, you've learned them all. A suggestion worthy of further investigation, no?
cues.zh: 当你试着读一个中音谱号、发现 C 现在跑到这里时，真的会把脑子绕晕。难道没人想到要改一改吗？嗯，想过，成千上万次。这是 1672 年 Thomas Salmon 牧师提出的方案，当年还小有名气。你有一个高音谱号，使用符号 TR，音域是 G 到 G；然后有一个中间谱号，音域相同；再有一个低音谱号，音域也相同。太好了！这样你学会一个，就等于全学会了。这个建议值得进一步研究，不是吗？

cues.en: Well, you'd think so, but when this proposal was published, it was ridiculed by musicians who submitted harsh rebuttals in subsequent publications. Reverend Salmon responded pretty angrily to this, and a 17th century Twitter war ensued. And this was a common reaction to proposed reforms throughout the 18th and 19th centuries. As Gardner-Reed put it, lengthy articles in the music press of the time even hold books attacking or defending various reforms of notation appeared with regularity.
cues.zh: 你大概会这么想，但这个方案发表后，音乐家们嘲笑它，并在后续出版物中提交了严厉反驳。Salmon 牧师对此反应相当愤怒，于是一场 17 世纪的 Twitter 大战随之而来。在 18 和 19 世纪，这是对改革提议的常见反应。正如 Gardner-Reed 所说，当时音乐媒体上的长篇大论，甚至攻击或捍卫各种记谱法改革的书籍，也频频出现。

cues.en: Many eminent musicians jumped into the verbal fray, adding their measure of prestige to extolling or denouncing one or the other of the new systems. This kind of hyper-resistance to change is not a good look and it does make me wonder whether we've lost out on some decent optimizations as a result of it. Of course, there's an inertia problem here. Notation is the standard. It's embedded in performance, theory, technology, etc. It's hard to change even when the suggestions are good.
cues.zh: 许多知名音乐家也加入这场口水战，为新体系中的这个或那个摇旗呐喊或猛烈抨击，也添上了自己的声望分量。这种对变革的过度抵制并不体面，也让我怀疑，我们是否因此错过了一些不错的优化。当然，这里有惯性问题。记谱法是标准，已经嵌入演奏、理论、技术等之中。即使建议很好，也很难改变。

cues.en: We'll address this problem in my conclusion, but for now, a bit of light relief. Let's look at a recent notation reform. MUTO METHOD The Muto Method is the creation of Japanese musician Wataru Okawa. He's a disruptor, but by no means are worst. Now before we go into detail, I should mention that whenever a proposed notation reform is published, it's almost always accompanied by what I'm gonna call a big massive whinge. A despairing indictment of how awful and illogical standard notation is.
cues.zh: 我们会在结论里处理这个问题，不过现在先轻松一下。来看一个近期的记谱法改革。MUTO METHOD Muto Method 是日本音乐家 Wataru Okawa 的创造。他是个颠覆者，但绝不是最糟的。在详细展开之前，我得提一句：每当有人发表记谱法改革方案，几乎总伴随着我所谓的“一大通巨型抱怨”。一种绝望的控诉，说标准记谱法多么糟糕、多么不合逻辑。

cues.en: The muto-methods hyperbole about notation is quite something. In this case, it's a grand conspiracy about how notation was intentionally designed to be difficult. Because, if I understand correctly, making it really difficult is effectively a form of encryption because it limits access for most people. I've not actually managed to make full sense of it yet. Back in the old days, aristocrats purchased scores. Then scores were played by performers.
cues.zh: Muto Method 对记谱法的夸张说法相当惊人。在这个例子里，这是一个大阴谋：记谱法是被故意设计得很难的。因为，如果我理解得没错，把它搞得特别难实际上就是一种加密，因为这限制了大多数人接触。我其实还没完全搞懂它。过去，贵族购买乐谱，然后乐谱由演奏者演奏。

cues.en: Aristocrats back then patronized their favorite performers and let them perform at salons regularly. These days, we enjoy music by playing encrypted song data on an iPod. The score back then is like encrypted song data now, and performers back then are like an iPod today.
cues.zh: 那时的贵族资助自己最喜欢的演奏者，让他们定期在沙龙演出。如今，我们通过用 iPod 播放加密歌曲数据来欣赏音乐。那时的乐谱就像现在的加密歌曲数据，而那时的演奏者就像今天的 iPod。

cues.en: From bottom to top, it represents one octave with the pitches arranged like this. So, no flatter sharp symbols, no clefs, fewer lines. Now, the eagle-eyed among you may notice that there are notes arranged in various positions between these lines. What's that about? Well, that's because there are actually two lines here and two lines here. But that's seven lines, you might say. No, because, as Muto Method helpfully explains, these blue lines are the ones you should imagine in your mind. That's useful, although one wonders why we should stop there.
cues.zh: 从下往上，它代表一个八度，音高像这样排列。所以没有升降号，没有谱号，线也更少。眼尖的观众可能已经注意到，线与线之间的各个位置都分布着音符。这是怎么回事？好吧，这是因为这里其实有两条线，这里也有两条线。你可能会说：可这不是七条线吗？并不是，因为正如 Muto Method 热心解释的那样，这些蓝线是你应该在脑海里想象出来的。挺有用，但让人纳闷的是，为什么只止步于此呢？

cues.en: Why not imagine everything in our minds? There's not really much to say about this reform, it's just a less good version of dozens of proposals that have come before, some of which I've already touched on. What I do want to address is that big whinge about aristocrats. That's worth digging into for a moment, because it reveals a very common association that standard notation suffers from. In my recent video about musical elitism, I spent a bit of time describing how classical music has an image problem. In one section, I discussed the general unfairness of musical education,
cues.zh: 为什么不把一切都在脑海里脑补出来呢？关于这种改良方案真没什么好说的，它不过是此前几十种方案的拙劣变体，其中一些我之前也提到过。我真正想探讨的，是针对贵族的那番大肆抱怨。这很值得深入探究一下，因为它揭示了标准记谱法经常背负的一种极其普遍的联想。在我最近一期关于音乐精英主义的视频里，我花了不少时间讲古典音乐的形象问题。在其中一节，我讨论了音乐教育中普遍存在的不公，

cues.en: using secondary schools in the UK as my example. In short, you're more likely to have a wide and varied musical education, including classes on how to read music, if your parents are wealthy. As a consequence, I often see notation itself associated with unfairness and elitism, which I think is just illogical. Imagine a world where only the wealthy could read and write. That would mean that most people in the English-speaking world would not be able to understand these symbols, which would be very unfair, but that unfairness would be social.
cues.zh: 并以英国的中学为例。简而言之，如果父母富有，你就更有可能接受广泛多样的音乐教育，包括学习如何识谱。结果就是，我经常看到记谱法本身被与不公和精英主义联系在一起，我觉得这完全不合逻辑。想象一个只有富人才能读书写字的世界。那就意味着英语世界的大多数人将无法理解这些字母符号，这确实极不公平，但这种不公是社会性的。

cues.en: The problem would not be the alphabet, it would be access. This is also true of musical notation. Today, it's simply not prioritized in education in the same way that reading and writing is, which means that children of low-income families are less likely to get an opportunity to learn it. But there's no quality in the alphabet or in notation that makes either elitist or exclusionary. Yet on multiple occasions, I've seen notation being held up as the culprit, which makes no sense to me. We don't do this for other things you need to study in order to master, like computer science.

cues.en: Farbegan Noten, or Coloured Notes, was published in 1888 by Christian Hoth. It starts with a lengthy treatise on the relationship between colours and pitch, culminating in a proposal that each of the 12 notes of the scale should have their own unique colour. But that's not all. Hoth goes into much more specific detail, proposing, for example, that the key of C major is 9 parts blue, 8 parts orange and 7 parts yellow. C minor is 7 parts green, 6 parts orange and 5 parts blue. The notation itself is represented as a grid.
cues.zh: 《Farbegan Noten》，又称《Coloured Notes》，于1888年由 Christian Hoth 出版。它开篇是一篇长篇论述，讨论颜色与音高的关系，最终提出音阶的12个音每个都应有自己独特的颜色。但这还不是全部。Hoth 还给出了更具体得多的细节，例如提出 C大调是9份蓝、8份橙、7份黄。C小调是7份绿、6份橙、5份蓝。记谱本身则用网格表示。

cues.en: Like many of the other proposals we've looked at, durations are relative, with durations represented by these curves. And since the grid is pretty tight horizontally, smaller durations get really physically cramped. The numbers here are meant to represent octaves, which makes sense because pitch is represented by color, so it doesn't need to be represented vertically. However, it gets pretty mind-bending because, for some reason, vertical placement can sometimes be ignored, and the same note can jump around vertically according to a logic I don't quite trust myself to adequately explain.
cues.zh: 和我们看过的许多其他方案一样，时值是相对的，并由这些曲线表示。由于网格横向相当紧，较短的时值在实际空间里会挤得厉害。这里的数字用来表示八度；这说得通，因为音高由颜色表示，所以不需要再用纵向表示。但它会变得相当费解，因为出于某种原因，纵向位置有时可以被忽略，而同一个音会按照一种我不敢说自己能充分解释的逻辑在纵向上跳来跳去。

cues.en: I think this means that Farbaga Noten is the only proposal which doesn't fit into either of the two fundamental types of notation identified by Hever. Now, rhythmically, this proposal matches a bunch of others we've looked at. However, the question of whether we'd be able to sight-read numerous colours at the same time and be able to interpret them reliably is one it's safe to say I'm skeptical about. We tend to use colour as an aid to other symbols, but rarely as the primary symbol itself. Gardner-Reed's assessment of this proposal is pretty amusing.
cues.zh: 我认为这意味着《Farbaga Noten》是唯一一个既不属于 Hever 所指出的两种基本记谱类型中任何一种的方案。从节奏上看，这个方案与我们看过的一堆其他方案相似。不过，我们是否能同时视读大量颜色并可靠地解读它们，这个问题可以说我持怀疑态度。我们通常把颜色用作其他符号的辅助，而很少把它本身当作主要符号。Gardner-Reed 对这个方案的评价相当有趣。

cues.en: Probably the most logical and convincing outright replacement reform I think I've seen. It was proposed by Julian Carrillo, an influential microtonal composer in 1895. First, the 12 pitches of the octave are represented by numbers. Middle range pitches are placed on the central line. If they're displayed on a lower space, they're an octave lower. Another space down, an octave lower again. A space up, an octave higher, etc. And that's it. No need for flat or sharp cymbals or clefs.
cues.zh: 大概是我见过的、最符合逻辑也最有说服力的彻底取代式记谱改革。它由 Julian Carrillo 于1895年提出，他是一位有影响力的微分音作曲家。首先，八度中的12个音高用数字表示。中音区的音高放在中央线上。如果它们显示在下方的一格，就低一个八度。再往下移一格，又低一个八度。往上移一格，就高一个八度，以此类推。就这样。不需要升降号或谱号。

cues.en: and it's way more vertically efficient, as can be seen by comparing this notated example with Carrillo's proposed system. For sure it would mean that we'd have to recalibrate our relationship to music theory. For example, you'd need to learn that 2-6-9 is a D major chord, 2-5-9 is a D minor chord, etc. It messes with our heads now, but it's completely sensible, and the numeric relationship would always be consistent. Another reason Carrillo created this system was so that it could accommodate different tuning systems and microtonality too.
cues.zh: 而且它在垂直方向上的利用效率高得多，对比这个记谱示例和 Carrillo 提出的系统就能看出来。当然，这也意味着我们得重新调整自己对乐理的认知。比如，你得记住 2-6-9 是 D 大调和弦，2-5-9 是 D 小调和弦，等等。现在看确实很让人抓狂，但逻辑完全合理，而且数字间的关系始终是一致的。Carrillo 创建这个系统的另一个原因，是为了同时兼容不同的律制和微音程。

cues.en: For example, using 24-tone equal temperament, or you could represent quarter tones with decimals or fractions, etc. The two probable downsides I can see are difficulties in understanding what key you're in, or in what key you're modulating to. But if I was to pick out the issue that might cause the most trouble, my guess is it would be how chords are visualised. I just don't know how easy it would be for a performer to chunk these numbers quickly, although I should mention that there are some types of non-Western notation that use numbers in this way.
cues.zh: 比如使用 24 平均律，或者用小数、分数来表示四分之一音等等。我能看出的两个潜在缺点是：很难判断当前处于什么调，或者正转调到什么调。但如果要挑出一个最让人头疼的问题，我猜会是和弦的视觉呈现方式。演奏者能不能快速将这些数字组块识别，我持怀疑态度，不过也顺便提一句，确实有些非西方记谱法会这样使用数字。

cues.en: We'd really need to see some serious comparative data to judge how successful Carrillo's system could be compared to standard notation, but even if it didn't compare well, it's an honorable attempt for sure. Now, as much as I'd love to spend another hour going through a ton of other systems, I do fear for your brain, so I thought I'd just cycle through a couple of other proposed reforms quickly before tying everything up in my conclusion. Hummingbird. This one is a relatively recent proposal, and I find it quite baffling.
cues.zh: 我们确实需要严谨的对比数据，才能评判 Carrillo 的系统相比标准五线谱到底算不算成功，但即便表现不占优势，这无疑也是一次值得尊敬的尝试。现在，虽然我很想再花一个小时盘点其他一堆系统，但我实在心疼大家的脑细胞，所以打算快速过一下另外几个改革方案，然后做个总结。Hummingbird。这是一个相对较新的提案，我觉得它让人非常费解。

cues.en: These weird balls have shading that indicates pitch, even though they're still represented vertically, a la standard notation. It's like the authors couldn't choose between one idea over the other, so just use both. The squiggly bits represent sharps or flats, durations have a little line which is meant to tell you how long they last. These extra adjacent lines indicate eighths. I think it's a total nightmare to look at. Perhaps at very early stages it might be useful, but it seems too messy and indistinct for anything beyond that. Stenographic notation, or...
cues.zh: 这些奇怪的圆球用阴影明暗来表示音高，尽管它们依然像标准记谱那样靠垂直位置来排布。感觉作者是在两种方案间拿不定主意，干脆全都用上了。扭曲的波浪线代表升号或降号，时值则用一条小线段来指示持续多久。旁边多出来的横线代表八分音符。看这玩意儿简直是噩梦。也许在入门启蒙阶段还有点用，但再往后走，它就显得太杂乱、太模糊了。速记谱，或者……

cues.en: Notation shorthand. This is not one proposal in particular. It's an entire genre. I'm not showing these here because I think they need to be assessed. I just think they're fun. In 1802, John Austen proposed these symbols for pitch and these symbols for duration, which would alter this notation to look like this. Another from Harry White in 1899 would represent this notation like this. And my favorite, in 1873, Alex M. C. Matt proposed the use of these symbols to represent pitch.
cues.zh: 乐谱速记。这并不是指某一个特定的提案，而是一整个流派。我把它们列出来并不是觉得有必要去评判，纯粹是觉得好玩。1802 年，John Austen 提出了这组表示音高的符号和这组表示时值的符号，原本的记谱就会变成这样。另一个是 1899 年 Harry White 的方案，会把这段谱记成这样。而我最喜欢的，是 1873 年 Alex M. C. Matt 提议用这些符号来表示音高。

cues.en: which means this notation would look like this. Global Notation is a recent proposal by Dr. Andrew Killick from the Department of Music at the University of Sheffield. Its purpose is to provide, quote, a more realistic picture of what listeners actually hear. By using a complex grid to represent pitch, pitch variation, note events and time, pitch is represented by synths and duration is, again, relative.
cues.zh: 这意味着这种记谱法看起来会是这样。Global Notation 是 University of Sheffield 音乐系 Dr. Andrew Killick 最近提出的方案。它的目的是提供——引用原话——“更真实地反映听众实际听到的内容”。它用复杂网格表示音高、音高变化、音符事件和时间，音高由合成器表示，时值同样是相对的。

cues.en: By being this technical and literal, it aims to be able to notate music from all cultures. It was initially proposed as a new way to write music, accompanied by the boilerplate notation wins you come to expect. However, from a performer's point of view, it is far less legible than many other proposals we've already looked at. One particularly awkward thing about it is how the staff lines change depending on the pitch ranges used.
cues.zh: 通过这种技术化、字面化的方式，它旨在能为所有文化的音乐记谱。最初提出时，它是作为一种新的音乐书写方式，还带着你早已习惯的那套模板化“记谱法优势”说辞。不过，从演奏者角度看，它比我们已经看过的许多其他方案都难读得多。一个特别别扭的地方是，五线谱的谱线会随所用音高范围而变化。

cues.en: which means the performer can never rely on memory to know what each line means in any given piece, so they'd have to constantly reference the sent numbers on the left to know what pitch they're supposed to play. Also, there's a weirdness in its basic premise. If it's supposed to represent what the listener actually hears, then the performance must have already happened, so it seems to me to be more of an aid to an existing audio recording rather than an instruction on how to perform in the first place, and the goals of global notation have narrowed since.
cues.zh: 这意味着演奏者永远不能靠记忆知道在任一作品中每条线代表什么，所以他们得不断参考左侧标注的数字，才知道该演奏什么音高。另外，它的基本前提也有点奇怪。如果它是要表示听众实际听到的内容，那演出必然已经发生，所以在我看来，它更像是现有录音的辅助工具，而不是一开始指导如何演出的说明；此后 Global Notation 的目标也收窄了。

cues.en: As of 2021, its stated purpose is purely academic, a tool to be used in the analysis of non-Western music. Certainly there are many cases where standard notation is insufficient, like in describing micro-variant textures found in Carnatic music, for example. So global notation is certainly a sensible proposal. Whether it will be successful as a system used in ethnomusicology remains to be seen. Jianpu is a straightforward system used successfully in early stage learning in China.
cues.zh: 截至 2021 年，它声称的用途纯属学术，是用于分析非西方音乐的工具。确实有很多标准记谱法不够用的情况，比如描述卡纳蒂克音乐中发现的微观变体织体。所以 Global Notation 当然是一个合理的方案。它能否作为民族音乐学使用的体系取得成功，还有待观察。Jianpu 是一个直截了当的体系，在中国早期学习阶段得到了成功应用。

cues.en: It's essentially a variation of the tonic sol fa system, where do re mi fa sol la ti are replaced by numbers. Dots are placed above or below to indicate whether the octave should be higher or lower. Although it superficially looks similar to Carrillo's system, it is completely different. More suitable for basic music, with obvious limitations once you go beyond that. However, it's really popular in China, so worthy of a deeper investigation as a potential early aid. So, after all this investigating, what conclusions can we come to?
cues.zh: 它本质上是首调唱名法体系的一个变体，其中 do re mi fa sol la ti 被数字取代。上方或下方加点表示八度应更高还是更低。虽然表面上看起来与 Carrillo 的体系相似，但其实完全不同。它更适合基础音乐，一旦超出这个范围就有明显局限。不过它在中国非常流行，因此值得作为潜在早期辅助工具深入研究。那么，经过这一番调查，我们能得出什么结论？

With Patreon, you generally get more stuff.

cues.en: Since it's clear that I haven't found a system I believe should replace standard notation, do we really have to just accept that things should never change? Well, no. As we've seen earlier, the development of notation happened very slowly for around 600 years, but it didn't stop two or three centuries ago. Various changes still slowly happen, with older, more ornate systems gradually becoming simplified. Now, in the 20th century, there was an explosion of adapted notation systems created to accommodate different types of music.
cues.zh: 既然显然我还没找到一套我认为能取代标准五线谱的系统，那我们真的只能接受一成不变吗？倒也不是。正如我们之前看到的，记谱法在大约 600 年的时间里演进得非常缓慢，但也并没有在两三百年前就停滞不前。各种演变依然在缓缓发生，早期更繁复的系统也在逐渐简化。到了 20 世纪，为了适应不同类型的音乐，更是涌现出了大量的改良记谱系统。

cues.en: microtonal music, free metered music and aleatoric music particularly stand out. I created a video about aleatoric music a few years ago if you're interested. There are also all kinds of bespoke scores like those created by Karlhein's Stockhausen which combined elements of standard notation with different types of graphic visualization to achieve specific musical effects. In these scores you can often spot many ideas from some of the proposals we've looked at in this video. There are also many kinds of abstract notation too.
cues.zh: 微音程音乐、自由节拍音乐和偶然音乐尤为突出。如果你感兴趣，我几年前做过一期关于偶然音乐的视频。此外还有各种定制乐谱，比如 Karlhein's Stockhausen 创作的那些，将标准记谱元素与不同形式的图形可视化结合，以达到特定的音乐效果。在这些乐谱中，你经常能看到本期视频探讨过的某些提议的影子。同时也有很多抽象记谱法。

cues.en: which introduce varying degrees of ambiguity to prompt novel types of musical performance. Some scores are works of art on their own right. However, the move to digital around the 80s and 90s was slow and clunky, and I also feel contributed to halting some of these 20th century developments, since digital applications simply couldn't accommodate much experimentation. This is true even today. However, digital apps will catch up, broadening the possibilities for what you can do by just being more flexible.
cues.zh: 它们引入了不同程度的不确定性，以启发全新的音乐演奏形式。有些乐谱本身就是艺术品。然而，在八九十年代转向数字化的过程既缓慢又笨重，我认为这也导致了 20 世纪这一波探索的停滞，因为数字化软件根本容纳不了太多实验性的尝试。即使在今天也依然如此。不过，数字化应用终将迎头赶上，通过提供更高的灵活性，为你拓展出更多可能性。

cues.en: And related to this point, let me jump into MuseScore to show you some of the things it can currently do. Here, I'm looking at a standard notation view, but if I make one little change, the same data is now displayed as guitar tab instead. I can also switch it to colored notation. I can switch it to solfege note heads. Just a few months ago, we released a version that works with braille readers, and we're currently developing the ability to display jianpu. The data is the same for all these formats, so switching between them is easy.
cues.zh: 说到这里，让我打开 MuseScore，带大家看看它目前能做些什么。这里是标准五线谱视图，但我只需做一点微调，同样的数据就会直接以吉他六线谱显示。我还可以把它切成彩色音符，或是切成唱名符头。就在几个月前，我们发布了一个支持盲文阅读器的版本，目前也正在开发支持简谱显示的功能。所有这些格式背后的数据都是相同的，因此在它们之间切换非常轻松。

cues.en: So what's needed now is further expansion to accommodate more systems and more flexibility. And this is where I think the change needs to happen. We need to move to a completely digital format. A format which, unlike PDF, retains and understands musical data. When that happens, musicians can choose whatever format they want. Chromatic staves, systems with relative durations, coloured notation, a piano roll, clever screbo, jianpu, the list goes on. The next logical step beyond that would see this format applied to digitized theory textbooks too.
cues.zh: 现在需要的是进一步扩展，以容纳更多记谱体系、提供更大灵活性。而我认为，变革就该发生在这里。我们需要转向完全数字化的格式——一种不同于 PDF、能够保留并理解音乐数据的格式。到那时，音乐家可以任意选择自己想要的格式。半音阶谱表、采用相对时值的体系、彩色记谱、钢琴卷帘、巧妙的 screbo、简谱，等等，不胜枚举。再往前推进一步，这种格式也顺理成章地可以应用到数字化的乐理教材上。

cues.en: This would weaken the need to agree on one unchanging system, and the price of introducing changes would be much lower because digital textbooks wouldn't need to be rewritten to accommodate them. You just add the latest standard. Now, all that aside, if you're not a person who reads notation, I hope I've successfully demonstrated that it's not something dead, which belongs to a bygone era. It's a living, breathing system that belongs to us now. It's also, frankly, nowhere near as hard to learn as some would have you believe, and learning it has enormously benefited my life.
cues.zh: 这会削弱必须约定一套不变体系的需求，引入变化的代价也会低得多，因为数字教材不必为适应变化而重写。你只需加入最新标准。撇开这些不谈，如果你不读谱，我希望我已经成功说明：它不是属于过去时代的死物。它是一个活生生、属于我们当下的体系。而且坦白说，它远没有某些人想让你相信的那么难学，学会它让我的人生受益匪浅。

cues.en: Despite its flaws and compromises, Standard Notation is a remarkable cultural achievement, universal for all instruments and which transcends spoken language barriers. A system that, just like the medieval chess game we saw at the beginning of this video, allows us to reach into the past to understand the ideas of our ancestors, a direct link to our history that's incredibly valuable and worth preserving. Notation will continue to change over the centuries and, for my money, won't be dying anytime soon.
cues.zh: 尽管有缺陷和妥协，标准记谱法仍是一项非凡的文化成就：它适用于所有乐器，并超越了口语障碍。这个体系就像本视频开头我们看到的中世纪棋局一样，让我们能够触及过去、理解祖先的想法，是一条与我们历史直接相连的纽带，极其宝贵，值得保存。记谱法会在未来几个世纪继续变化；在我看来，它短期内不会消亡。
